rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 – statewide rent increase cap (blocked from ballot)
rules.requirement: The proposed ballot initiative would have repealed the state ban on rent control and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC ruled it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law.
rules.key_value: lesser of CPI or 5% annual cap (not enacted)
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, and dwelling units in facilities operated solely for educational, religious, or nonprofit purposes.
rules.conflict_note: Proponents say the defect is easily fixable and may re-file; no rule in force.

no_rule_findings.finding: Massachusetts still has its statutory ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P); the proposed repeal and statewide cap was blocked from the ballot, so no rent cap exists at state or local level.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases for most residential rental units.

parsed.doc_summary: Law-firm blog post reporting that the Mass. SJC in Cella v. Attorney General (SJC-13893) kept Initiative Petition 25-21 (statewide rent cap) off the November 2026 ballot because of its religious-facility exemption; the G.L. c. 40P ban on rent control remains.
